review_target: server/internal/service/access_test.go (16 test cases across 15 top-level funcs, 3 with subtests) against tasks/2.md's TDD Anchor, tech-spec.md Decisions 3/5/10/11 and the Data Models section, and the house style set by costing_test.go. Code already exists (TDD: tests-then-implementation) — reviewing whether the suite is a meaningful specification of AccessService's behavior, not whether it happens to pass.
summary: All 10 TDD Anchor items are present with matching names and none are weakened; the implementer added 6 more (unknown-login on GetAccessState, EnsureUser non-reset delegation, infra-error-not-misreported-as-conflict, flag-write-failure-blocks-decide, and the 6-case invalid-argument table) that close real gaps the anchor list left implicit. Assertions are substantive throughout — exact call counts and captured arguments on both stubs (ensureCalls/setAccessCalls/decideCalls/createCalls), not just 'err == nil', plus stored-state checks after each operation. The Grant/Revoke tests using different decidedBy values ('rogogdbd' vs 'second-admin') is a real safeguard against an argument-mixup false pass, verified in the code. The accessRequestRepoStub returning ErrConflict directly from CreateRequest (rather than modeling RowsAffected 0/1/2) is not a stub/reality divergence risk: Task 2's own task file explicitly assigns the RowsAffected→ErrConflict translation to the repository layer (Task 3), and tech-spec's testing strategy independently plans a repository-contract suite (access_repo_test.go, run against both MemoryRepository and PostgresRepository) that re-verifies the real RowsAffected semantics — so the fidelity question is correctly scoped away from this task. Two things are worth the team's attention, neither blocking: (1) SetAccess decides whether to call DecideRequest off the RequestStatus snapshot taken in the earlier GetUser call rather than a fresh check; this is architecturally intentional (UserRecord.RequestStatus is documented as exactly this join) and switching to a second round-trip via GetRequest would not remove the underlying non-transactional TOCTOU window anyway, but there IS a genuine race — a CreateRequest landing between SetAccess's GetUser and DecideRequest calls creates a pending row that will never get decided (has_access stays correct/authoritative per Decision 3, so no security impact, but the row lingers forever with no way to reach it again since CreateRequest short-circuits once access exists) — this trade-off isn't called out in the code comment or covered by any test, and isn't easily testable at the stub level since it requires state mutation between two sequential calls inside one method; (2) the implementer's summary overstates coverage — it claims 'empty/whitespace login on all four methods' but only EnsureUser gets both empty and whitespace subtests; GetAccessState, CreateRequest, and SetAccess are only exercised with the empty-string case. Functional risk is low since all four route through the same shared requireLogin() helper, but the report should be corrected to match what's actually in the file. The implementer's claim that ListUsers/GetRequest are correctly out of Task 2's scope checks out against the task file's own 'What to do' list (no ListUsers passthrough is required on AccessService) and against the API contract (AccessState/UserRecord carry no DecidedBy/DecidedAt, so no planned consumer needs GetRequest) — this looks more like unused interface surface at the tech-spec level than a Task 2 gap, and is out of this task's authority to resolve.

findings.description: SetAccess (access.go:158-191) reads UserRecord once via GetUser, writes the access flag via UserRecord.SetAccess, then decides whether to call AccessRequestRepository.DecideRequest purely from the RequestStatus captured in that first GetUser call (line 179: `if user.RequestStatus == "" { return nil }`) — it never re-reads request state before deciding. If a user's CreateRequest lands concurrently, in the window between the admin's GetUser and DecideRequest calls, the resulting pending request row is invisible to this SetAccess call and is never decided by it. Because CreateRequest short-circuits to ErrConflict without touching the repository once hasEffectiveAccess() is true (access.go:146-148), that pending row can never be resubmitted into visibility either — it is permanently stuck at 'pending' with no further code path that revisits it. has_access remains correct and authoritative (Decision 3), so there's no access-control/security consequence, but it is a real, silent data-consistency artifact a future 'list pending requests' admin view would surface incorrectly. Using UserRecord.RequestStatus instead of a second AccessRequestRepository.GetRequest round-trip is the right call architecturally (that's literally what the join in UserRecord's doc comment is for), and a fresh GetRequest call immediately before DecideRequest wouldn't actually close the race either, since nothing here is transactional across the three repository calls — so this is a structural trade-off of the whole non-transactional design, not a defect specific to this implementation choice.
findings.recommendation: Not a blocking fix for Task 2 (whose own scope is rule logic on stubs, not transactional guarantees). Two options for the team to consider going forward: (a) add a one-line comment at access.go:179 making the trade-off explicit — 'known race: a request created between GetUser and here is left undecided; has_access remains authoritative regardless (Decision 3)' — so a future reader doesn't have to rediscover it; (b) if the dangling-pending-row UX matters later, Task 3/4's repository layer could make DecideRequest itself a conditional UPDATE keyed on 'any pending row for this login' rather than relying on the service to know a row exists, closing the gap without adding a round trip. No test change is required from this review; a stub-level regression test for this race isn't practical without introducing artificial concurrency into the stubs, which would be disproportionate to the risk.

findings.description: accessRequestRepoStub tracks a getCalls counter (access_test.go:116) that is never asserted anywhere in the file. Nothing in the suite explicitly locks in that SetAccess/CreateRequest never call AccessRequestRepository.GetRequest — the fact that they don't is only an emergent property of reading the source, not something a regression in a future edit (e.g., someone 'helpfully' adding a fresh GetRequest lookup inside SetAccess) would be caught by.
findings.recommendation: Add `if requestRepo.getCalls != 0 { t.Fatalf(...) }` to the two or three SetAccess/CreateRequest tests where the design intentionally avoids a GetRequest round-trip (e.g. TestAccessService_SetAccess_Grant_SetsFlagAndApprovesRequestWithDecidedBy and TestAccessService_SetAccess_NoExistingRequest_DoesNotCallDecideRequest). Cheap addition, makes the 'decide off the GetUser snapshot, not a second read' design decision from finding #1 an enforced invariant rather than an implicit one.

findings.description: The implementer's summary states the invalid-argument coverage is 'empty/whitespace login on all four methods, empty decidedBy' (6 subtests). Checked against TestAccessService_InvalidArguments_ReturnErrInvalidArgumentWithoutRepoCalls (access_test.go:542-586): the 6 actual subtests are 'EnsureUser с пустым логином', 'EnsureUser с пробельным логином', 'GetAccessState с пустым логином', 'CreateRequest с пустым логином', 'SetAccess с пустым логином', 'SetAccess без указания администратора'. Only EnsureUser gets both an empty-string and a whitespace-only variant; GetAccessState, CreateRequest, and SetAccess are each tested only with the empty-string case, not whitespace. The description in the handoff overstates what's covered.
findings.recommendation: Low risk in practice — all four methods route through the same shared requireLogin() (access.go:199-207), so a whitespace-only bug would almost certainly show up via the EnsureUser whitespace case too. Still, either correct the report's wording to 'whitespace tested via EnsureUser (shared validator)' or, if the team wants belt-and-suspenders per-method coverage, add three more one-line whitespace subtests (GetAccessState/CreateRequest/SetAccess) to the same table — cheap given the table-test structure already exists.

findings.description: Sanity-checked the implementer's claim that ListUsers/GetRequest are legitimately out of Task 2's scope, deferred to Task 4/5's admin-list endpoint. Confirmed for ListUsers: tasks/2.md's 'What to do' section lists exactly EnsureUser/GetAccessState/CreateRequest/SetAccess as AccessService methods to implement — no ListUsers passthrough is asked for, so its absence isn't a Task 2 gap. For GetRequest, the claim is directionally right (Task 2 correctly doesn't need it) but the deeper premise — that Task 4/5 will need it — is not obviously true from the tech-spec as currently written: the AccessState DTO (GET /api/v1/access/me) and UserRecord DTO (GET /api/v1/admin/users) both carry RequestStatus/RequestedAt but neither carries DecidedBy/DecidedAt, and the tech-spec's own description of the admin list endpoint ('возвращает всех пользователей с has_access, role, request_status') doesn't mention needing decision metadata. So it's plausible GetRequest ends up unused by any handler for the whole feature, which would make it dead interface surface rather than a method 'needed later'.
findings.recommendation: No action needed in Task 2 — this is a tech-spec-level question, and the interface signature is fixed by Data Models regardless (task explicitly says to implement 'точно по сигнатурам'). Worth a one-line flag to whoever executes Task 4/5: confirm GetRequest actually gets called by some handler, or note in decisions.md that it remains reserved/unused by design.
